description: RFC 8785 (JCS) cross-language conformance corpus for the AEP v3 receipt canon (citadel-cli#1021). Each case: `input` is raw JSON fed to the canonicalizer; `jcs` is the expected RFC 8785 output; `sha256` is sha256(jcs) as lowercase hex. `sha256_16` (when present) is an INDEPENDENT reference from docs/design-canon-framework.md section 9.2 -- a three-library run (Go gowebpki/jcs + Python jcs + Python rfc8785) -- so matching it is real cross-language evidence, not Go self-consistency. Go verifier: `go test ./internal/aep -run TestJCSConformanceCorpus`. Python verifier (future, aceteam #9287): for c in cases: assert rfc8785.dumps(json.loads(c['input'])) == c['jcs'].encode(); assert hashlib.sha256(rfc8785.dumps(json.loads(c['input']))).hexdigest() == c['sha256']. Regenerate jcs/sha256 with -update-golden (which asserts every committed sha256_16 still matches).

cases.name: collision_pair_a
cases.note: v1 newline-canon collision pair, half A: engine has an embedded newline. Under the v1 newline-delimited canon this collides with collision_pair_b to identical signed bytes (design section 9.4); under JCS the newline is escaped as backslash-n inside the string and the two are DISTINCT.

cases.name: collision_pair_b
cases.note: v1 newline-canon collision pair, half B: model has an embedded newline. Distinct from collision_pair_a under JCS.

cases.name: number_int_one
cases.note: score as JSON integer 1. Canonicalizes identically to number_float_one -- JCS numbers are value-based, so the transport hop that erases Go's float-ness is harmless (design section 3.2 / P3). Matches the design section 9.2 v2-receipt-subset row.

cases.name: number_float_one
cases.note: score as JSON float 1.0. Same canonical bytes as number_int_one.

cases.name: number_two_thirds
cases.note: score = 2/3, the shortest round-tripping double 0.6666666666666666. design section 9.2.

cases.name: runtime_doubles
cases.note: Nine runtime-computed doubles spanning the 1e21 / 1e-6 notation boundaries (arrays are not key-sorted). design section 9.2. Note 123456789012345680000 is a FLOAT that renders in fixed notation with no decimal point -- fed raw to the canonicalizer, not through the integer-domain check.

cases.name: key_order_utf16
cases.note: Object keys sorted by UTF-16 code units (input deliberately scrambled). The emoji U+1F600 sorts BEFORE the fullwidth tilde U+FF5E because its leading surrogate 0xD83D < 0xFF5E. design section 9.2.

cases.name: null_empty
cases.note: null / empty-string / empty-array / empty-object all preserved (RFC 8785 does NOT drop null map values, unlike the trust canonical_json port). Input scrambled to prove sorting. design section 9.2.

cases.name: string_escaping
cases.note: ECMAScript JSON.stringify escaping: short escapes for the quote, backslash, and the newline/return/tab/backspace/formfeed controls; NO HTML escaping of < > & (Go encoding/json would emit backslash-u003c etc., normalized away by the JCS round-trip); raw UTF-8 for non-ASCII (accented e and emoji). Self-consistent case (no cross-language reference pinned).
